title: No Swayamvara at the Bow
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1(65-66, 72-75) (Critical Edition; vulgate 1.66-67, 73-76)

captions.instagram:
Was there really a swayamvara for Sita?

On Vivah Panchami we remember the wedding of Rama and Sita. Many of us picture a grand swayamvara: kings gathered, the bow, Sita with the varmala, and Parashurama storming in. That is how Goswami Tulsidas tells it in the Ramcharitmanas. In Valmiki's Ramayana, Janaka had declared Sita 'vīryaśulkā': her bride-price is valour. Kings had come earlier, couldn't even lift the bow, and besieged Mithila for a year. Rama came with Vishvamitra only to see the bow, lifted it as if in play, and broke it in the middle. Parashurama meets them later, on the road home after the wedding. Both are told with devotion. Happy Vivah Panchami.

Which scene did you grow up with: the swayamvara or the visit? 👇 Jai Siya Ram!

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1(65-66, 72-75) (Critical Edition; vulgate 1.66-67, 73-76)

Was there really a swayamvara for Sita?

On Vivah Panchami we remember the wedding of Rama and Sita. Many of us picture a grand swayamvara: kings gathered, the bow, Sita with the varmala, and Parashurama storming in. That is how Goswami Tulsidas tells it in the Ramcharitmanas. In Valmiki's Ramayana, Janaka had declared Sita 'vīryaśulkā': her bride-price is valour. Kings had come earlier, couldn't even lift the bow, and besieged Mithila for a year. Rama came with Vishvamitra only to see the bow, lifted it as if in play, and broke it in the middle. Parashurama meets them later, on the road home after the wedding. Both are told with devotion. Happy Vivah Panchami.

Which scene did you grow up with: the swayamvara or the visit? 👇 Jai Siya Ram!

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1(65-66, 72-75) (Critical Edition; vulgate 1.66-67, 73-76)
Verses:
• The princes came to see the bow — 1.65.5-6
• Sita's bride-price is valour (vīryaśulkā) — 1.65.15
• Kings came earlier and could not grasp or lift the bow — 1.65.16-20
• The kings besieged Mithila for a full year — 1.65.21-23
• If Rama strings the bow, Janaka will give Sita — 1.65.27
• Vishvamitra tells Rama to look at the bow — 1.66.12
• Rama: I will touch the bow and try to lift or draw it — 1.66.14
• Before thousands of men, Rama strung it as if in play — 1.66.15-16
• He drew it full and broke it in the middle — 1.66.17
• Thunder and earthquake; all fell except the sage, the king and the two princes — 1.66.18-19
• No varmala in Valmiki's bow and wedding chapters; the only garland is on the bow — 1.66.2; 1.65-72
• Janaka gives Sita's hand: 'This is Sita, my daughter, your companion in dharma' — 1.72.17
• Parashurama meets them on the road to Ayodhya after the wedding — 1.73.7-22
• Ramcharitmanas: Sita places the jayamala on Rama — Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand (before doha 264)
• Ramcharitmanas: ten thousand kings tried at once; Parashurama arrives on hearing the bow broke — Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand (before doha 251, 268)

verify_note: CE 1.65.5-6: the princes wish to SEE the bow. 1.65.15, 17: Sita is vīryaśulkā (valour her bride-price). 1.65.16-20: kings came earlier, couldn't grasp or lift the bow. 1.65.21-25: they besieged Mithila a full year; gods gave Janaka an army; they fled. 1.65.27: if Rama strings it, I give Sita. 1.66.12-14: Vishvamitra 'look at the bow'; Rama 'I will touch it, try to lift or draw it'. 1.66.15-17: takes it playfully, thousands of men watching, strings it, draws it full, breaks it in the middle. 1.66.18-19: thunder, earthquake; all fall except sage, king, two Raghavas. No garland in 1.65-72 except on the bow (1.66.2). 1.72.17: the kanyadaan verse. 1.73.1-22: after the wedding, on the road to Ayodhya, Parashurama appears; 1.74-75 the challenge. Manas Bal Kand: 'भूप सहस दस एकहि बारा' (before 251); 'सियँ जयमाल राम उर मेली' (before 264); 'तेहिं अवसर सुनि सिवधनु भंगा। आयउ भृगुकुल कमल पतंगा' (before 268).
